analysis:
The supplied units are .github/scripts/test-threat-budget.py. Unit :3 is base text for lines 564-1079; unit :4 is head text for lines 1-565. They are offline CI tests for the review-budget and Bedrock transport code. The changes visible in the patch excerpt are an `os` import, a `WRITE_ATTEMPTS` constant used in assertions, a `ConcurrentHTTPServer` with `request_queue_size=32` for the barrier-based contention fixture, and new or modified tests (conflict-burst recovery, 12 simultaneous writers, ledger conflict exhaustion, and more). The head ranges 1034-1061 and 1177-1301 lie outside the supplied head text, so I could not inspect them.

The tests assert fail-closed behavior: invalid budget modes, unwritable ledgers, settlement failures, and missing fallback cost halt spending. They also assert that diagnostics exclude provider payloads, that bounded write attempts are enforced, and that final uncertainty never clears the merge gate.

This is test-only code that talks to a local 127.0.0.1 fixture server with synthetic credentials. It adds no production attack surface. It does not touch any provider, coordinator, or native runtime code covered by the canonical threat model (TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-011, T-041 and others).

The T-041 definition is unrelated to these changes. I identified no regression.

The remaining uncertainty is the production behavior behind the new `WRITE_ATTEMPTS` constant and conflict retry logic in threat_review/state.py. That file was not supplied, so the tests cannot confirm its fail-closed behavior. The head portions after line 565 were also not supplied.
